newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-German shares hit record, dollar strong.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-German shares hit record, dollar strong.

text.p: German shares powered to a record close on Monday, building on last week's rally with help from the strong dollar and hopes of another cut in interest rates.
Europe's other major bourses spent a mostly weak session, although the Paris bourse managed to eke out a small gain by the close of business.
London, in contrast, spent the day well adrift and closed 19.5 points, or 0.48 percent, down on concerns about sterling's strength and fears that British interest rates are set to rise.
The Dow Jones Average was down around 38 points, but off its lows, by the time European bourses closed.
The dollar traded at up to six-week highs against the mark in European trading, buoyed by Swiss franc weakness and gaining extra support from stronger than expected U.S. economic data.
The Swiss currency fell to a 23-month low against the dollar at 1.3145 Swiss francs, undermined by the view that continued economic weakness will keep Swiss interest rates low.
A much stronger than expected reading of the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Mangement (NAPM) index helped underpin the dollar, although signals on inflation remained muted.

"The data is still in line with moderate non-inflationary growth, but recent statistics have hinted at some acceleration in (economic) activity," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist Europe at Bank of America in London.
The dollar rose against the mark after France and Germany reiterated their commitment to a stable franc-mark rate and renewed speculation about a possible cut in German interest rates.
The British pound briefly hit 2.6002 against the mark, its highest level since February 1994, before slipping slightly.
Among European equity markets, the German bourse was the star, although Oslo's Total share index also hit a record high.
Germany's DAX index of 30 leading shares hit a new bourse record of 2,860.24 points in early trade, before paring gains to close up 13.08 points, or 0.46 percent, at 2,858.60 points.
In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX recouped some Wall Street induced weakness to end 4.62 points up at 2,853.46.

Analysts had not been expecting the 2,850 point level to be breached until the end of the year. The DAX has rallied three percent in the last week, boosted by the dollar's strength, which benefits German exporters.

A major casualty was carmaker Volkswagen AG, however. VW ended floor trade down almost five percent, or 29.50 marks, at 587 marks after investors sold stock on worries about the company's legal dispute with U.S. carmaker General Motors Corp over allegations of industrial espionage.
London investors marked prices down as they fretted over the strength of sterling and interest rates. Yet many traders and strategists said they still held out hope for a year end rally.

The FTSE 100 index ended 19.5 points lower at 4,038.5, as decliners beat advancers by a margin of about two to one. Second-liners fared a bit better, with the FTSE 250 losing 13.7 points to settle at 4,414.8.

"It's pretty much a forgone conclusion that (UK monetary authorities) will put up rates by 0.25 to 0.50 percent by January or February," said one dealer. "To what degree that's priced into the market, I don't know."
French shares closed a little firmer, rebounding from some consolidation during the morning.
Traders said strength in bonds and hopes of interest rate cuts in France and Germany gave investors reason to be cheerful.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 2.97 points or 0.13 percent at 2,318.63, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,322 from 2,319 on Friday's close.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.80 yen and 1.5436 marks against 113.90 yen and 1.5320 marks in late Europe on Friday. The pound stood at 1.6839 to the dollar against 1.6813 on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS - CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares closed down 19.5 points, or 0.48 percent, at 4,038.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index ended up 2.97 points at 2,318.63.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 13.08, or 0.46 percent, at a record 2,858.60. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX ended up 4.62 points at 2,853.46.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $371.05 against $371.35. Silver finished a cent lower at $4.72.
